sentences.text:
Arvind Tripathi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March,
2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:17777
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Himanshu Joshi

On The 5 th Of March, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 6240 of 2026
 Arvind Tripathi
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Ankit Saxena - Advocate for applicant.
 Ms. Manisha Singh - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/S
 Shri Ashwajit Gautam - Advocate for respondent no.2.
 Order

Petitioner has filed this petition under Section 528 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for quashing of FIR dated 12.01.2019, contained in Annexure-A/1, registered at Crime No.25 of 2019 at Police Station-Saman, District - Rewa (M.P.) against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 120-B and 409 of Indian Penal Code.
2. During pendency of petition before this Court, parties have amicably resolved their dispute.
Respondent No.2 has filed application under Section 359(2)(5)(9) of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for compounding of offence.
It is submitted that offence registered against the petitioner are compoundable.
3. Joint prayer is made by the counsel for the the parties for quashing of proceedings.
It is submitted by them that offence said to have been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17777 2 MCRC-6240-2026 committed by petitioner is a civil dispute between the parties.
Now, parties have settled their differences.
Offence alleged to be committed by petitioner does not touch upon the society or larger interest of public and State.
Complainant no longer want to prosecute the case against the petitioner.
In these circumstances, no useful purpose will be served by keeping criminal case pending before the trial Court.
4. Case was sent for recording of statement and verification of compromise application before Registrar (Judicial-II).
Before Registrar (Judicial-II), petitioner has submitted original Aadhar Card for establishing his identity and further counsel for petitioner has identified the petitioner.

sentences.text: Complainant has also submitted his Aadhar Card and he has also been identified by his counsel.
Affidavit of complainant has also been filed along with the application.
Parties were questioned by Registrar (Judicial-II) and they had stated that compromise is done voluntarily with free will without any threat or inducement.

5. Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that compromise has been reached between the parties and offence alleged to have been committed by petitioner will not affect the society at large and offence is principally civil dispute between the parties, application filed for compromise i.e. I.A. No. 3066 of 2026 is allowed.
6. In view of aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, petition is allowed.

FIR dated 12.01.2019 registered at Crime No.25 of 2019 at Police Station-Saman, District -Rewa (M.P.) for committing offences under Sections 406, 420, 120-B and 409 of Indian Penal Code and consequential NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17777 3 MCRC-6240-2026 proceedings arising out of it are quashed.

7. However, it is made clear that the amount deposited by the applicant before the learned concerned trial Court in compliance of order dated 11.04.2015 passed in M.Cr.C.No.12884 of 2019 be released in favour of the applicant in accordance with law.
8. Certified copy as per rules.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE rk.
